title: productionDeployPorts composes the durable target reader and the release decision, replacing two null stubs
description:
PRODUCER ROW filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-06 at governor-afbde490's 13:50Z direction, from worker-f72a1438's step-1 audit and qa-4f771bb8's 13:41Z re-measure of task-84cd2e55aae942cf8d56657308215fde. That parent's dependsOn names this row.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD. `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-command.ts:91` `productionDeployPorts()` returns:
  docker: nodeDockerRunner,
  releaseDecision: () => null,
  ssh: nodeSshRunner,
  target: () => null,
  transfer: nodeImageTransfer,
TWO OF THE FIVE ARE NULL STUBS, not one. The governor's note named `target`; `releaseDecision` is stubbed the same way and has the same consequence.

WHAT EACH STUB COSTS:
- `target: () => null` means a PRODUCTION deploy can never find where to deploy. `deploy-ports.ts:41` declares `DeployTargetPort = (environment) => DeployTarget | null` with the comment "WRITTEN by `deployment.set_target`; only read here". task-358b6ec8ee884ca6b6bc96bbf1f54d84 lands that write and its `DeployTargetPort` implementation; this row COMPOSES it into production. Until then every production deploy refuses DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING regardless of what an operator bound.
- `releaseDecision: () => null` means a PRODUCTION deploy always reports "no release decision", even when Gate 3 approved one. `deploy-ports.ts:48` declares `ReleaseDecisionPort = (environment, sha) => string | null` with the comment "Gate 3 is a sibling row; reading a decision here is a read, and deciding one would be inventing authority this row does not hold." The engine's DoD 7 requires it to CITE the decision when one exists - a permanent null makes that clause unsatisfiable in production while its unit test passes on an injected port.

THIS IS COMPOSITION ONLY. Do not change how the engine executes, do not reshape `moe-deploy-receipt/1` (task-da60dc4b builds against it), and do not implement Gate 3 - reading a decision is a read.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN ROW: the engine, the target write and Gate 3 are three landed-or-landing rows owned elsewhere, and this is the one place their production wiring meets. An injected port in a unit test proves the engine; only this composition proves the daemon.
definitionOfDone: `productionDeployPorts()` returns a real `target` backed by the durable target reader that task-358b6ec8 lands - NOT `() => null`. Assert through the PRODUCTION composition that a bound target is found: bind one, then read it back through `productionDeployPorts().target(environment)` and assert the DeployTarget members. A unit test with an injected port does not discharge this.

`releaseDecision` reads the goal's Gate 3 decision and returns its id when one exists, null when none does - and BOTH are asserted. A permanent null makes the engine's 'cites the release decision' clause unsatisfiable in production while its injected-port test stays green, which is exactly the gap this row closes.

READING ONLY, NEVER DECIDING: `releaseDecision` reads an existing decision and never creates, approves or infers one - Gate 3 belongs to task-2a345b2e97d94599b4688af1923056e5. Assert that an environment with no decision yields null rather than a fabricated or defaulted id.

AN UNBOUND ENVIRONMENT STILL YIELDS null from `target`, and the engine's DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING refusal still fires - assert the refusal with its code AND layer through the composed path, so composing a real reader does not accidentally make every environment look bound.

NO ENGINE CHANGE: `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-receipt-contracts.ts` is EMPTY. task-da60dc4b (rollback) resolves through that receipt shape and task-04b3ce7e owns the engine's wiring.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file.
taskRails: COMPOSITION ONLY. This row wires landed readers into `productionDeployPorts()`; it changes no engine behaviour, no receipt shape and no refusal order.
READING A DECISION IS A READ. `releaseDecision` never creates, approves or infers a Gate 3 decision - deciding one would invent authority this row does not hold (deploy-ports.ts:48).
BOTH STUBS, NOT ONE. `target` and `releaseDecision` are both `() => null` at HEAD and both are this row's.
PROVE IT THROUGH THE PRODUCTION COMPOSITION. An injected port in a unit test proves the engine, not the daemon - that gap is why this row exists.

ARCHITECT RE-MEASURE AT HEAD (architect-d6d49adc, 2026-09-07). Global rail "stale by default", GAP-CLAIMED-PRESENT direction: this row's gap is CLOSED. Both stubs are gone; no implementation slice remains. I am NOT submitting a plan — planning it would re-implement a landed surface owned by a DONE row and an owner commit, in a shared worktree.

MEASUREMENT 1 — `target` is NOT `() => null`.
`apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-command.ts:101-112` implements the durable reader: readEvents(deployTargetAggregateId) -> filter DEPLOY_TARGET_BOUND_EVENT -> .at(-1) -> decodeBoundedJsonBytes -> decodeDeployTarget, with catch -> null ("Store failure means UNKNOWN, never permission to reuse a stale/default target").
Landed by `git log -S DEPLOY_TARGET_BOUND_EVENT -- deploy-command.ts` = 1faef6a3 feat(task-79f8c7c00efe447a922f42b1967c3968) — this row's OWN dependsOn entry, status DONE. That row was created 13:52:45Z; this row 14:02:10Z. Same architect, ten minutes apart, same subject: this row is the later duplicate.

MEASUREMENT 2 — `releaseDecision` reads a real decision in the production path.
`deploy-command.ts:99` still reads `releaseDecision: () => null`, but that value NEVER reaches the deploy engine. `deploy-command.ts:221-233`: `const ports = options.ports ?? { ...productionDeployPorts(store, projectId), releaseDecision: (_environment, sha) => { ... readReleaseReceipt(store, projectId, releaseReceiptId(projectId, goalId, sha, "RELEASED", null)) ... } }` — the spread is OVERRIDDEN. Landed by 4ac0dbda "fix: harden release and deployment review gaps" (owner out-of-band, no Moe-Task trailer).
It is a READ, never a decide: returns receipt.receiptId on ok, null on RELEASE_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND, throws DomainRefusal on any other code. Gate 3 (task-2a345b2e, WORKING) keeps its authority.
The only production read of `ports.releaseDecision` is `deploy-service.ts:210`, inside deploy(). `rollback-command.ts:149` composes `productionDeployPorts(store, projectId)` bare, but rollback never reads that port — so line 99's stub is unreachable in deploy and unread in rollback. `task-79f8c7c0` DoD 5 ruled it deliberate and required saying so; changing it now would contradict a DONE row.

DoD, item by item, all already true at HEAD:
1. target through the PRODUCTION composition — `deploy-journey.test.ts:179-181`: `productionDeployPorts(context.store, PROJECT_ID).target(PRODUCTION)` `toStrictEqual(LOCAL)` + `Object.isFrozen`, after the real `deployment.set_target` setter binds it.
2. releaseDecision BOTH directions — `deploy-release-binding.test.ts:59-65` asserts `releaseDecision: receiptId`; `:67-74` asserts null across `it.each(["missing","other goal","other SHA","refused"])`. Both drive `createDeployCommandHandler` with NO `ports` option, so line 221's production composition is the surface under test; only host effects (nodeDockerRunner/nodeSshRunner/nodeImageTransfer/nodeDeployBuild) are mocked. It cannot pass against `() => null`.
3. no decision -> null, never fabricated — the "missing" arm above; plus `:76-89` refuses a corrupt matching receipt with RELEASE_RECEIPT_INVALID before any effect.
4. unbound env -> null + DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING with code AND layer — `deploy-journey.test.ts:185-191`: `expect([refusal.code, refusal.layer]).toEqual([DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING, DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP])` with `docker.calls` empty, `it.each([false,true])` over staging-bound — exactly the "don't make every environment look bound" clause.
5. no engine change — nothing to change.
6. gate: `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/deployment/deploy-release-binding.test.ts src/deployment/deploy-journey.test.ts` from apps/daemon -> `Test Files 2 passed (2)` / `Tests 26 passed (26)`, 5.79s.

NO MUTATION DRILL RUN, and I am not claiming one. The composition is proven by construction instead: the binding test passes no `ports`, so it exercises `deploy-command.ts:221` and asserts the receipt carries the recorded release receipt id — an arm that `() => null` cannot satisfy. I judged a tracked-file mutation in this shared checkout (26 foreign dirty paths, active peer sweeps) not worth the sweep-commit risk for signal already available by reading the seam.
